summary: Mars Survival Nav is a first-principles, resource-constrained (76 KB binary sector packs, 508 KB active RAM) 3D/4D Martian Extravehicular Activity (EVA) navigation and science operations engine built for astronauts and flight controllers. While orbital maps view Mars at regional kilometer scales, an astronaut on foot experiences a hyperlocalized 2.05 km × 2.05 km survival problem governed by suit center-of-gravity slope limits, low-thermal-inertia eolian sand traps, moving canyon shadows, UHF radio blackouts, and GPS-denied positional drift. Built on real NASA MOLA/HRSC elevation, THEMIS thermal inertia, SHARAD subsurface ice radar, and Curiosity/Phoenix surface imagery across 4 candidate landing sites, our engine couples 4D moving-sun A* routing with xEMU PLSS life-support physics (O₂, SWME cooling water, suit battery), bidirectional walkback isochrones, autonomous 2-hop UHF relay placement, 3D subsurface stratigraphic curtains, and live mid-EVA hazard re-routing.

What It Does & How It WorksMars Survival Nav is a first-principles, resource-constrained (76.0 KB binary sector packs, 508.0 KB active TypedArray RAM, 25.4 KB gzipped core bundle) 3D/4D Martian Extravehicular Activity (EVA) navigation and science operations engine. While orbital maps view Mars at regional kilometer scales, an astronaut on foot experiences a hyperlocalized 2.05 km × 2.05 km survival problem governed by suit center-of-gravity slope limits, low-thermal-inertia eolian sand traps, moving canyon shadows, UHF radio blackouts, and GPS-denied positional drift.

7 Core Engineering Innovations Beyond Standard Pathfinding

  1. 4D Spatio-Temporal Anisotropic A Routing in (x, y, z, t):* Evaluates directional slope climbing vs. downhill braking costs, eolian sand sinkage (TIU < 140), boulder roughness, sky-view radiation exposure, and moving-sun arrival hour t(node) so multi-hour traverses do not get trapped in -95°C dusk canyon shadows.
  2. Coupled 3-Consumable xEMU PLSS Telemetry: Tracks metabolic O₂ (180 L tank), Spacesuit Water Membrane Evaporator (SWME) sublimator cooling water (4.2 L tank), and suit battery (850 Wh) dynamically scaled by carried NASA science instrument mass (kg).
  3. Bidirectional Anisotropic Walkback Isochrone Field (WALKBACK): Runs dual outbound and reverse-edge return Dijkstra wavefronts (accounting for +3 kg of collected rock cores on the return climb) in under 10 ms to project the 95 L Point-of-No-Return survivability boundary onto the 3D terrain.
  4. GPS-Denied Navigation Uncertainty (CEP) & Optical Skyline Triangulation: Models 2-way UHF radiometric ranging (±0.8 m CEP) when Habitat line-of-sight is locked, optical skyline triangulation off high-prominence horizon peaks (±2.4 m CEP) in radio blind spots, and IMU dead-reckoning drift rings (+2.8% per meter walked).
  5. Autonomous 2-Hop UHF Relay Viewshed Optimizer (DEPLOY RELAY): Solves for the single traversable ridge crest that maximizes 2-hop UHF radio coverage (Habitat ↔ Relay ↔ Astronaut), boosting canyon comms coverage up to 88%+ and collapsing positional CEP drift.
  6. 3D Volumetric Subsurface Stratigraphic & SHARAD Curtain (3D STRATA) + Unconformity Detector (DISCOVERY): Extrudes a 3D underground cross-section beneath the active route revealing SHARAD water-ice depth horizons and dipping Hesperian/Noachian beds, paired with a 5×5 Shannon-entropy lithologic contact detector.
  7. Steiner Point Rover-Foot Rendezvous & Live In-Situ Hazard Re-Routing (Shift + Click): Routes a wheeled utility rover (≤14.5° slope limit) to haul heavy drills to an optimal Rendezvous Basecamp (R*) while the astronaut scrambles the final cliff unburdened with a 2.2 kg hand kit, and supports instant mid-EVA obstacle re-routing via Shift + Click.

Quantitative Benchmark Results Across 4 Mars Landing Sites

  • Mount Sharp (Gale Crater Boxwork Ridge): 76.0 KB disk | 508.0 KB RAM | WP-1 Max Slope: 13.5° (Smart A*) vs. 45.1° (Naive Direct) | Sand Traps: 0 m vs. 278.1 m | Max CEP: ±3.5 m | SHARAD Ice: -6.2 m | A* Compute: 3.72 ms | Full Loop (HAB → WP-2 → WP-1 → WP-3 → HAB): 4.66 km, 139.7 L O₂ | Walkback Reachable: 75% | 2-Hop UHF Relay Gain: 76% → 88%
  • Deuteronilus Mensae (Fretted Glacial Dichotomy): 76.0 KB disk | 508.0 KB RAM | WP-1 Max Slope: 14.5° (Smart A*) vs. 18.0° (Naive Direct) | Sand Traps: 0 m vs. 330.3 m | Max CEP: ±7.0 m | SHARAD Ice: -1.6 m | A* Compute: 4.19 ms | Full Loop (HAB → WP-2 → WP-1 → HAB): 3.89 km, 110.67 L O₂ | Walkback Reachable: 85% | 2-Hop UHF Relay Gain: 34% → 48%
  • Arcadia Planitia (Starship Candidate Site AP-1): 76.0 KB disk | 508.0 KB RAM | WP-1 Max Slope: 4.6° (Smart A*) vs. 29.5° (Naive Direct) | Sand Traps: 0 m vs. 387.7 m | Max CEP: ±13.8 m | SHARAD Ice: -1.5 m | A* Compute: 2.59 ms | Full Loop (HAB → WP-1 → WP-2 → HAB): 3.55 km, 90.15 L O₂ | Walkback Reachable: 96% | 2-Hop UHF Relay Gain: 32% → 57%
  • Phlegra Montes (Lobate Debris Apron PM-1): 76.0 KB disk | 508.0 KB RAM | WP-1 Max Slope: 19.1° (Smart A*) vs. 29.0° (Naive Direct) | Sand Traps: 0 m vs. 0 m | Max CEP: ±12.7 m | SHARAD Ice: -1.4 m | A* Compute: 3.56 ms | Full Loop (HAB → WP-1 → WP-2 → HAB): 4.18 km, 129.36 L O₂ | Walkback Reachable: 60% | 2-Hop UHF Relay Gain: 41% → 73%

Tools, Languages & Hardware Target Built from scratch in TypeScript, Three.js / WebGL, Vite, and Node.js using flat TypedArray binary buffers (Float32Array, Uint16Array, Uint8Array) with zero runtime heap allocations during A* search, engineered to run within a 4,096 KB embedded spacesuit wrist co-processor RAM budget.
